video_title: Crypto is Growing Up ft. Theo
gist: Iggy, a former hedge fund manager and Polygon Ventures investor now working at tokenization startup Theo, argues that real-world-asset tokenization only matters when the tokenized asset is genuinely usable on chain — priced, lendable, pledgeable, composable — rather than 'tokenization theater.' He walks through Theo's stack (the THbill onchain money market fund, now powered by Fidelity after Wellington; yield-bearing tokenized gold; and THUSD, gold plus a short CME gold-futures contango harvest), and lays out why he thinks tradfi is in bubble territory, why Bitcoin has no near-term catalyst, and why commodities benefit from the AI data-center capex wave.

insights.claim: Theo pivoted from funding-rate arbitrage to real-world assets because onchain capacity ran out — there was no way to generate high yields on chain at scale — while RWAs offer roughly two orders of magnitude more capacity relative to onchain capital.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Explains the hard capacity ceiling on basis-trade yield products and why credible onchain yield increasingly has to be imported from off-chain markets.

insights.claim: Stable coins at roughly $300 billion are the first generation of RWAs — effectively tokenized dollars — with a further $30 billion to as much as $300 billion of other real-world assets on chain depending on whether repos are counted.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Sizes the base for tokenized yield products and shows how elastic published 'RWA TVL' figures still are when underwriting the sector's growth rate.

insights.claim: Emerging markets are ahead of the US in blockchain payments for the same reason they leapfrogged landlines to mobile — developed markets already have a system that mostly works, so there is less urgency, while chains like stable and Polygon become the settlement backbone for neobanks and fintechs.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Payment-chain volume and stablecoin growth should concentrate outside the US; US-centric adoption metrics will understate the trend.

themes.theme: Bitcoin positioning and the gold flow reversal

insights.claim: Bitcoin has no near-term catalyst and sentiment is not washed out — across 30-plus tracked metrics positioning reads neutral, and options skew has moved from massive put skew a couple of months ago back to the middle, implying no panic selling and probably no bottom yet.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: A tactical argument against buying this Bitcoin drawdown yet; watch for a genuine put-skew blowout as the capitulation trigger.
insights.quote: so it's like you can't really say that there is a panic selling of Bitcoin which is why we're probably not at the bottom yet in the near term

insights.claim: The substitution between Bitcoin ETFs and gold ETFs has reversed: Bitcoin ETFs pulled inflows out of gold ETFs at launch, but recently gold has reclaimed the 'digital gold' allocation, even as Bitcoin ETF inflows turned positive in July on almost every day.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Treat gold and Bitcoin ETF flows as competing for the same debasement-hedge dollar; the relative flow trend is a tradable sentiment gauge.

insights.claim: Institutions remain broadly positive on Bitcoin and selectively on Hyperliquid, Ethereum (the default chain for RWAs) and Solana's fundamentals, but many institutional mandates still cannot buy cryptocurrencies at all — while institutional interest in blockchain infrastructure is unconstrained and massive.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: The blockchain-versus-cryptocurrency divergence means institutional capital reaches tokenized products and rails well before it reaches most tokens.

insights.claim: Traditional-finance heavyweights have converted to tokenization: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said stable coins could reach $3 trillion (10x today's ~$300 billion), Larry Fink calls tokenization the future of finance, and Stan Druckenmiller has said dollar flows will move to stable coins because they are faster and cheaper.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Endorsement from old-school macro and asset-management legends lowers the career risk of institutional allocations to tokenized cash, a leading indicator for flows.
insights.quote: in 10 years that all the the dollar floors are going to stable coins faster and cheaper

themes.theme: Stable coins vs yield-bearing onchain cash

insights.claim: A composable onchain money market fund is strictly better than a non-yielding stable coin because the holder captures the 3.65% risk-free rate — about one basis point per day — instead of ceding it to the issuer.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Idle stablecoin balances are a pure transfer from holder to issuer; composable yield-bearing substitutes should structurally erode issuer float income.
insights.quote: you're getting one basis point a day exactly because Fed funds rate is 3.65 and there are 365 days a year

insights.claim: Even so, the majority of RWA value will remain in stable coins for the next two to three years because Tether and USDC have multi-hundred-billion scale, deep fintech and neobank integrations, brand recognition and presence across dozens of chains.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Tempers the bear case on stablecoin issuer economics: share loss to yield-bearing assets is a grind, not a cliff.

insights.claim: Settlement assets need to be non-yield-bearing for technical reasons — during the settlement window it is ambiguous who earns the accrued interest — so yield-bearing tokens such as BUIDL or THUSD will win as collateral rather than as settlement money.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Defines a durable niche for non-yielding stablecoins and points investors to collateral share, not settlement share, as the metric for yield-bearing tokens.

insights.claim: The most plausible long-run alternative settlement asset is a non-yield-bearing tokenized gold, ironically the opposite of Theo's own yield-paying gold token.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: A non-consensus candidate to watch if dollar-stablecoin settlement dominance is ever contested.
insights.quote: for technical reasons it's probably going to be ironically the non-yield bearing tokenized gold

insights.claim: 'Tokenization theater' is when an issuer tokenizes an asset, issues a press release and announces TVL while the asset is merely recorded on chain and never used; the real opportunity requires onchain pricing, liquidity, lending, collateral, fractionalization and looping — finance as open-source software.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: A concrete screen separating RWA announcements from RWA businesses: measure onchain usage rather than headline TVL.
insights.quote: this is what I call tokenization theater uh where people have some asset, they tokenize it, they issue a press release, they announce TVL, and then technically it's on it's recorded on chain but it doesn't use blockchain

insights.claim: Succeeding in RWAs requires a team that is simultaneously crypto-native, fluent in tradfi finance, and strong enough in engineering to architect the systems — an 'RWA trilemma' that most of the few hundred RWA teams reviewed at Polygon Ventures failed, having only two of the three.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: A diligence filter for RWA startups that explains the sector's high announcement-to-execution failure rate and why very few RWA investments were made at Polygon.
insights.quote: I've met many teams and and most of them had two out of three.

insights.claim: Velocity — volume divided by TVL — is the metric that matters for tokenized assets, and Theo's THbill became the number one onchain money market fund by velocity while reaching four chains and more than 15 DeFi protocols within two weeks and over $200 million in TVL, including the fastest-growing RWA Morpho market and fastest growth on Arbitrum.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Gives a usage-based KPI to rank tokenized products in place of easily inflated TVL, and a benchmark for what onchain product-market fit looks like.
insights.quote: one of my favorite metrics is what are called velocity is volume divided by TVL

insights.claim: Whitelisted, KYC-gated tokenized products accessed through a web2 login are not real democratization of finance, whereas cryptocurrency itself is already fully permissionless and globally accessible.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Sets a distribution bar that most compliant tokenization ventures do not clear — and that bar is where the retail growth actually lives.
insights.quote: when you launch uh products on chain and then whitelisted and it's still like KYC and you have, you know, you have to access it through like a a regular web two login platform, then that's not really not really democratization

themes.theme: Gold: leasing yield, contango harvest, capacity

insights.claim: Most of tradfi is in bubble territory — very high valuations and very narrow credit spreads — which is why Theo deliberately launched bear-market assets, treasury bills and gold, after reviewing several dozen assets others had tokenized and judging them poor investments cyclically.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: A practitioner explicitly avoiding credit-linked tokenized products at current spreads — a caution flag for tokenized private credit and CLO-style RWA offerings.
insights.quote: most of the things in Chhatfi are in kind of a bubble territory. Doesn't mean that they the bubble cannot inflate for for a bit more, but the valuations are really high. The credit spreads are very narrow.

insights.claim: Theo generates native yield on tokenized gold by leasing out the underlying metal while the token holder retains title (the analogy used is a rental apartment or car lease), flipping gold from an asset that bleeds carry — a GLD-style ETF costs 40 basis points a year — into one that pays.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Turns gold's structural negative carry into yield; the hidden risks to underwrite are lessee credit and title enforcement, not price.

insights.claim: THUSD is a gold-backed yield coin built as tokenized gold plus a short in CME gold futures, stacking the gold leasing yield on top of harvested contango, with investment rather than payments as the primary use case.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Returns depend on gold staying in contango and on leasing spreads — the two variables to monitor when underwriting or replicating this structure.
insights.quote: it's kind of a yield sandwich where you get the gold native yield and you get another yield from shorting the future

insights.claim: About $30 trillion of gold has ever been extracted at current prices, but most of it never moves — central banks in particular rarely sell — so the tokenized-gold opportunity should be sized against the investment-gold slice that has grown since 2023, where $1 trillion would be only about 3% of the market.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Separates reachable from unreachable gold demand and gives a concrete runway estimate for a tokenized-gold franchise.

insights.claim: Gold trades over a trillion dollars per day in genuine, non-wash volume — a few hundred billion each in futures, OTC and non-CME exchanges — making its capacity effectively unlimited relative to a total crypto market of a couple of trillion.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: The scalability case for gold-based onchain strategies: unlike crypto basis trades, the underlying market will not constrain AUM growth.
insights.quote: So gold trades over a trillion per day,

themes.theme: Fidelity deal, onchain demand, retail endgame

insights.claim: Theo won a Fidelity partnership for its THbill money market fund after about a year of work and years of failed attempts by the same people at Polygon, with Fidelity (roughly $7 trillion AUM) choosing Theo on the strength of its onchain velocity and composability track record plus a couple hundred million of TVL — while Wellington remains a second provider for vendor diversification.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Large tradfi managers are now selecting tokenization partners on demonstrated onchain usage, turning usage metrics into a business-development moat.
insights.quote: So our team has worked on it since last summer. It took a year

insights.claim: Onchain capital's current demand is a quadrilemma — short duration, extremely safe, high-single-digit yield, and fully transparent — and existing options fail it: crypto-backed loans are not fully transparent, and tradfi mortgages and CLOs trade at extremely tight spreads with unclear direction.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: A four-way screen for judging any onchain yield product, and a warning that tight-spread tradfi credit is being repackaged on chain without adequate compensation.

insights.claim: AI is deflationary long term for human capital and software, but the data-center capex buildout is inflationary now — visible in construction, land, electricity and water costs — so commodities should benefit for the next two years because AI cannot create more gold, silver, copper or near-term power.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: The stated rationale for Theo's next product line being commodity-focused, and a broader macro trade: long physical-constraint commodities against AI-disrupted labor and software.
insights.quote: AI cannot create more gold for example I cannot create more more silver or copper

insights.claim: Theo has over 80,000 unique customers in more than 60 countries, but the money follows a steep Pareto curve dominated by the top 20 or 30 whales, with retail as a long tail that grows only over a five-to-ten-year horizon.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: Near-term revenue for onchain yield products is whale- and institution-driven; retail is a long-dated option that should be modeled as such.
insights.quote: we have over 80,000 unique customers in more than 60 countries

insights.claim: The long-term vision is giving anyone globally the portfolio previously reserved for private-bank clients — cheap beta in gold, stocks and treasuries plus a slice of structured product, with no minimums — which is the point at which people come on chain to invest rather than to speculate.
insights.speaker: Iggy (Theo)
insights.so_what: If executed, this compresses the private-wealth fee stack; tokenized structured products are the disruption vector to watch for high-minimum wealth offerings.
insights.quote: So what gets me excited is you can have you know a farmer in Thailand have a proper portfolio just like a high net worth bank.
